experiments.why: A two-token query where only Rain Jacket has both words, so the switch from every to some also returns Down Jacket and Rain Boots.
A two-token query no product fully matches, which now returns every jacket and the Gore-Tex shell through OR plus alias expansion.
A single plain token, which should still return exactly the two jackets.
A misspelling with no alias entry, which must still find nothing.
A query that differs from Women's only by the apostrophe, which must still find nothing.
The new jckt alias, which used to find nothing and now returns both jackets.
The new goretex alias, which now matches the hyphenated Gore-Tex product.
A query that is an inherited Object property name, so ALIAS_MAP[token] returns a function and spreading it throws where the old code returned the product.
Configured category facets first, then the unconfigured weight in its original place.
An empty category order, so the default order alone decides.
A category facet with a higher displayOrder number that still outranks every default facet.
A configured facet that is not available, which must not appear in the result.
